findings.message: newPeriod only rewrites the one period in force on `effectiveOn`. Periods that already start later keep the old department, grade, manager, contract and salary, so the change is quietly undone when the next period starts. The fixtures plant these later periods for the 6 part-timers who go full time (FULL_TIME_FROM). Fix: also apply `set` to every hr.employment row with `starts_on > on` for this person, or reject the change when later periods exist. Add a variant test for: no later period, one later FTE step, and two later steps.
findings.scenario: Engineering filler i=60 has periods (joined, fte 0.5) and (2026-12-01, fte 1). changePerson({department:'Quality', managerEmployeeNo:'LL-0291'}) effective 2026-10-17 → from 2026-12-01, CURRENT, getEmployment and listEmploymentPeriods show Engineering and the old manager again.

findings.message: recordLeaver ends only the periods with `starts_on <= leftOn`. A period that starts after the leave date keeps `ends_on = null`, so the leaver still looks employed in that period with no end. This hits a future FTE step and also a 'joining' person who leaves before their start date. Fix: delete those later periods, or end them too, and test both variants.
findings.scenario: Part-timer with a 2026-12-01 FTE-1 period → recordLeaver leftOn 2026-11-15 → listEmploymentPeriods still returns {startsOn:'2026-12-01', endsOn:null, fte:1}, and allocations counts capacity for someone who has left. Same for addPerson joinedOn 2026-12-01, then recordLeaver leftOn 2026-11-20.

findings.message: Person status is decided once, at write time. The module has `jobs: []`, so nothing ever moves a person from 'joining' to 'active' once joinedOn passes, or to 'left' once a future leftOn passes. Headcount, the directory chips, 'upcoming', reportUserIds and listPeople({status}) all go stale. The module standard says waiting work must be a @amax/workflows schedule. Fix: add a daily job that applies the transitions through a service, or derive status from the dates when reading.
findings.scenario: recordLeaver({employeeNo:'LL-0417', leftOn:'2026-11-30'}) on 2026-10-17 → on 2026-12-15 Kasun is still 'active', counts in headcount 184 and stays in Maya's `reports` scope. Rifkhan (joining 2026-11-02) still shows 'Joins Nov 2' in December.

findings.message: Person-level fields (title, location, workEmail) are written to hr.person straight away, whatever `effectiveOn` says. Yet the hr.person.changed event and the audit `after` both record them as effective on that date. Fix: reject effectiveOn for person-only fields, or schedule them, and make the event reflect what actually took effect.
findings.scenario: change_person({employeeNo:'LL-0417', title:'Tech lead', effectiveOn:'2027-01-01'}) → the title shows 'Tech lead' today, while the event says changed:['title'], effectiveOn:'2027-01-01'.

findings.message: entityOf resolves free text with `name ilike %entity%` and `order by name limit 1`. Input that matches several legal entities, or that contains a `%`/`_` wildcard, silently picks the alphabetically first one. The person is then created in that entity's employee series and currency. Fix: match exactly on id, country or name, and fail when there are zero matches or more than one.
findings.scenario: add_person entity:'Lumen' (or 'Labs', or '%') in a tenant with 'Lumen Labs Australia' and 'Lumen Labs Sri Lanka' → the person is created in Australia with AUD currency and an AU-00xx number.

findings.message: getEmployment gives unmasked pay and bank data (salary, EPF, bank account) to any caller that passes the string "system". Nothing authenticates that claim and nothing audits the read. architecture.md says contract reads 'apply the caller's data scope', but any module or chat/MCP code path can call it with "system". listPeople, getPerson and listEmploymentPeriods also take no viewer at all. Fix: take a ServiceContext or a real system actor that core issues, check it, and audit unmasked reads.
findings.scenario: Any module code calls getEmployment(tx, id, "system") while serving a PM's request → that PM receives Kasun's base salary 285000 and bank account 8001207740 unmasked, and no audit row records the read.

findings.message: nextEmployeeNo claims numbering is 'serialised per tenant' through pg_advisory_xact_lock, but no test runs two addPerson calls at once. A single-session test stays green if the lock is deleted. Add a race test with two real sessions that asserts two distinct, consecutive numbers.
findings.scenario: Delete the pg_advisory_xact_lock line → hr.test.ts still passes, while two concurrent add_person calls both compute LL-1190 and one fails on unique (tenant_id, employee_no).

findings.message: inScope skips the legal-entity scope check whenever viewerOf(ctx) returns nothing. Any context without a viewer (an agent, a workflow, or a contract command) therefore gets unscoped HR writes. Fail closed: when there is no viewer, check the actor's scope another way or reject.
findings.scenario: A ServiceContext with no viewer, acting for an HR role limited to Australia, runs recordLeaver({employeeNo:'LL-0417'}) → a Sri Lankan record is changed with no entity check.

findings.message: An unknown `/hr/e/:entity` code falls back to entity=undefined and renders the whole company under that URL. Commit 0853a72 fixed only the client-side select, not the server route. Legal entities are also keyed by country code, so two entities in the same country share a code and the second is unreachable. Fix: return notFound() for an unknown code, and give each entity a unique key.
findings.scenario: GET /hr/e/nz → '184 people in 2 entities', with the full directory under an NZ URL. A tenant with two LK entities → /hr/e/lk always shows the first one.

findings.message: 'Employment in force' is written three times, and the copies use different clocks. CURRENT (contracts.ts:44) uses the DB's `current_date`. peopleStats' departments lateral uses the JS `today` passed in. getEmployment uses `new Date().toISOString()` (UTC). The directory, the department chart and the employment card can therefore disagree around midnight and in tests. Fix: use one parameterised SQL fragment that takes the as-of date, everywhere.
findings.scenario: DB timezone Asia/Colombo, 2026-11-30 19:00 UTC, a department change effective 2026-12-01 → the directory and getPerson show the new department (current_date = Dec 1), while the 'People by department' chart and the Employment card still use the old one (Nov 30).

findings.message: Entity names and country mappings are hard-coded in three places: chat options ['Sri Lanka','Australia'], COUNTRY in services.ts, and COUNTRY in ui/parts.tsx. The department list in chat.ts is fixture data. A tenant with other entities cannot pick them through chat. Other duplicated helpers can also drift: initialsOf (services.ts and fixtures/index.ts, which doesn't trim) and day() (contracts.ts and queries.ts, with different falsy handling).
findings.scenario: A tenant adds an NZ entity → the 'Add person' intent cannot offer it, and countryName shows the raw entity name.

findings.message: Gaps against the module standard: there is no `db/schema.ts`, and no a11y tests (both required). The contract tests don't check the PersonJoined or PersonLeft payloads. The contract also exports CURRENT (raw hr.* SQL) and toPersonRef, which the README's contract list doesn't mention and which expose internals to other modules.

The AC-3 expectations depend on the wall clock, because the services use the real today(). From 2026-12-01, addPerson with joinedOn '2026-12-01' returns 'active', so the expected status 'joining' fails. Fix: inject today into the services, or use dates relative to now.
The 'all' view caps the directory at 1000 rows and drops the Show all link, so a directory over 1000 is cut off with no way to reach the rest.
findings.scenario: A tenant with 1200 people → /hr/all shows 'Showing 1000 of 1200' and has no link to the remaining 200.

findings.message: `employment.ends_on` stands for two things: the end of an effective-dated period (set by newPeriod and the FTE steps) and the end of the contract. contractsEndingNextMonth counts any fixed-term period boundary as a contract ending. EmploymentCard shows the period end as 'ends <date>' even on permanent contracts. Fix: store the contract end in its own column (or on the person), or count and show only the last period's ends_on.
findings.scenario: A fixed-term person gets change_person(grade, effectiveOn 2026-11-15) → the old period gets ends_on 2026-11-14 and the lede says one more contract ends in November. A permanent 0.5-FTE engineer's card reads 'Permanent, part time, 50%, ends Nov 30'.

findings.message: getEmployment returns unmasked pay, EPF and bank details to any caller that passes the string literal "system". This is a public contract, so any module (including its MCP or chat tools acting for a user) can bypass 002 masking by typing one string. Fix: require an unforgeable system capability (for example a token from @amax/core that only workflows and the runtime can mint), or expose a separate, audited system read.
findings.scenario: Another module's read tool runs `getEmployment(tx, id, "system")` for a PM viewer → that PM sees Kasun's salary 285000 and bank account 8001207740.

findings.message: One hr.document retention entry labels every document 'health' and deletes it, whatever the row's own class (personal, pay, performance). The classes in the retention manifest therefore don't match the data. Add one entry per document class, or document why a single rule covers them all.
